hello.note: Also: Hallo. Casual: Heisann! or Hei hei! Formal, e.g. in an office: God dag.

goodbye.note: Short and very common: Ha det! Casual: Hei hei! or Snakkes! (talk soon).

please.note: Can sound pleading. In everyday requests Norwegians add takk instead: En kaffe, takk.

thank_you.note: Warmer: Tusen takk (a thousand thanks) or Takk skal du ha.

youre_welcome.note: Also common: Ingen årsak. When handing something over, say Vær så god.

yes.note: To say yes to a negative question, use jo: Kommer du ikke? – Jo!

sorry.note: Also very common: Beklager. For real regret: Jeg er lei for det.

excuse_me.note: Often just Unnskyld, followed by your question: Unnskyld, vet du hvor stasjonen er?

good_morning.note: Casual: Morn! Many people also use Morn as a quick hello later in the day.

how_are_you.note: Norwegians say du to almost everyone; the formal De is now rare. Also: Hvordan går det?

im_fine.note: Shorter: Bra, takk! To ask back: Og du?

whats_your_name.note: The h in hva is silent: 'va HAY-ter doo'. Du is polite enough, even with strangers.

my_name_is.note: Jeg sounds like 'yai'. More formal: Mitt navn er …

nice_to_meet_you.note: Often just: Hyggelig! Also common: Hyggelig å hilse på deg.

where_from.note: The h in hv- words is silent: hvor sounds like 'voor'.

speak_english.note: Most Norwegians speak English well. Start politely: Unnskyld, snakker du engelsk?

dont_understand.note: Also common: Jeg skjønner ikke. To ask someone to repeat: Hva sa du?

speak_slowly.note: Norwegian softens requests with litt (a bit) rather than a word for please. Also: langsommere.

where.note: Said 'voor'. Where to? is hvor hen? Where from? is hvorfra?

what.note: Said 'va'. Hva? alone can sound blunt; to ask someone to repeat, say Unnskyld? or Hva sa du?

when.note: Å sounds like the 'aw' in law: 'nawr'.

why.note: Said 'VOOR-for'. Also common in speech: Hvorfor det?

who.note: Said 'vem'. Don't mix it up with hvor (where).

where_bathroom.note: Casual: Hvor er doen? Signs say WC; Damer = women, Herrer = men.

can_you_help.note: The h in hjelpe is silent: 'YEL-peh'. Extra polite: Kunne du hjelpe meg?

what_time.note: Also written and said: Hva er klokken? Both are correct.

what_means.note: Also common: Hva vil det si?

one.note: With neuter nouns it is ett: ett glass. Written én when stressed, to tell it from the article en.

seven.note: Syv is also correct and very common in speech.

eight.note: Å sounds like the 'aw' in law: 'AW-teh'.

water.note: Tap water is good to drink. In a café: Kan jeg få et glass vann?

bread.note: The d is silent: 'brø'. Ø is like the vowel in French deux.

menu_please.note: Kan jeg få …? is the everyday polite way to ask for anything. Short form: Menyen, takk.

bill_please.note: Short form: Regningen, takk. For the whole table: Kan vi få regningen?

delicious.note: Also: Deilig! or Nydelig! About a whole meal: Dette var kjempegodt!

no_meat.note: Or: Jeg er vegetarianer. Kj is a soft hiss, like the ch in German ich.

enjoy_meal.note: A host often says Vær så god! (help yourself). After eating, guests say Takk for maten!

right.note: Not 'correct', which is riktig. Turn right: Ta til høyre.

straight_ahead.note: Also spelt rett frem. Both are correct.

stop_here.note: Also very natural: Du kan slippe meg av her (you can let me off here).

airport.note: Official names and signs often use lufthavn, as in Oslo lufthavn.

hotel.note: Double l, stress on the end: ho-TELL.

train_station.note: In everyday speech: togstasjon, or just stasjonen. Oslo's main station is Oslo S.

want_to_go.note: Norwegian can drop the verb go here. Also very common: Jeg skal til … (I'm going to …).

is_it_far.note: Also: Er det langt herfra? (from here)

one_ticket.note: Return ticket: tur-retur. In many cities you buy tickets in an app.

too_expensive.note: Haggling is not usual in Norwegian shops, except at flea markets (loppemarked).

cheaper.note: Asking about the shop's range: Har dere noe billigere? (dere = you, plural)

id_like_this.note: For a neuter noun: dette. When buying, also common: Jeg tar denne.

just_looking.note: Also: Jeg bare ser meg litt rundt.

pay_card.note: Cards are taken almost everywhere, and some places no longer accept cash.

cash.note: To pay in cash: betale kontant.

closed.note: Signs also say Lukket. Most shops are closed on Sundays.

big.note: With neuter nouns: stort (et stort glass). Plural: store.

small.note: Irregular: lite with neuter nouns (et lite glass), små in the plural.

tomorrow.note: Morgen alone means morning. Tomorrow morning: i morgen tidlig.

later.note: Also spelt seinere. Afterwards: etterpå. Soon: snart.

good_evening.note: Hei works at any time of day, too.

good_night.note: Also said when parting late at night. Leaving earlier in the evening: Ha en fin kveld!

see_you_later.note: Also: Ses senere! Tomorrow: Vi ses i morgen! Casual: Snakkes!

wait_moment.note: Also: Bare et øyeblikk. Casual: Vent litt!

every_day.note: The h is silent: hver sounds like 'vair'.

call_police.note: In Norway dial 112 for the police, 113 for an ambulance, 110 for the fire brigade.

need_doctor.note: Lege is used for both male and female doctors.

im_lost.note: On foot. When driving: Jeg har kjørt meg vill.

dont_feel_well.note: Also: Jeg er ikke helt i form. Ill: Jeg er syk.

hospital.note: Out of hours, for urgent but not life-threatening problems, go to the legevakt.

lost_phone.note: Mobil is the everyday word for a mobile phone. Telefonen also works.

allergic.note: E.g. allergisk mot nøtter (nuts), melk (milk), gluten.

be_careful.note: Sudden warning: Pass på! or Se opp!

i_like_it.note: About food, also: Det smaker godt.

dont_like_it.note: Also common: Det liker jeg ikke.

im_happy.note: Glad is the everyday word for happy. Deeply happy: lykkelig.

congratulations.note: On a birthday: Gratulerer med dagen!

my_family.note: Also: min familie, which puts more weight on min (my).

mother.note: In everyday speech: mamma (mum). My mother: moren min or min mor.

father.note: In everyday speech: pappa (dad). My father: faren min or min far.

brother.note: Plural: brødre. Big brother: storebror, little brother: lillebror. Siblings: søsken.

sister.note: Plural: søstre. Big sister: storesøster, little sister: lillesøster.

child.note: Same in the plural: ett barn, to barn. Son: sønn. Daughter: datter.

friend.note: A female friend is often venninne, though venn works for both. Boyfriend or girlfriend: kjæreste.

this_is_my_friend.note: For a female friend: Dette er venninnen min. Also common: Dette er en venn av meg.

are_you_married.note: Many couples live together unmarried: samboer means live-in partner.

have_children.note: Asking a couple: Har dere barn? (dere = you, plural)

monday.note: Days take no capital letter. The g in -dag is silent: 'MAN-dah'. On Monday: på mandag.

sunday.note: Most shops are closed on Sundays.

weekend.note: Also common in speech: weekend. Have a good weekend: God helg!

what_day.text: Hvilken dag er det i dag?
what_day.note: The h is silent: 'VIL-ken'. The date: Hvilken dato er det i dag?

next_week.note: Last week: forrige uke. This week: denne uka (or denne uken).

fifteen.note: Other teens: tretten (13), fjorten (14), seksten (16), sytten (17), atten (18), nitten (19).

twenty.note: Tj is the soft hiss of German ich. The older form tyve is still heard. 21: tjueen.

thirty.note: Tens and units are written as one word: trettifem (35).

fifty.note: The other tens: førti (40), seksti (60), sytti (70), åtti (80), nitti (90).

hundred.note: Also: ett hundre. Two hundred: to hundre.

thousand.note: As in tusen takk, 'a thousand thanks'. Written with a space: 1 000.

years_old.note: Longer form: Jeg er … år gammel. År sounds like 'awr'.

red.note: The d is silent: 'rø'. With neuter nouns: rødt (et rødt hus).

blue.note: With neuter nouns: blått (et blått hus).

green.note: With neuter nouns: grønt (et grønt hus).

yellow.note: Say 'gool'. With neuter nouns: gult (et gult hus).

black.note: Sort is also correct. Same form with neuter nouns: et svart hus.

white.note: The h is silent: 'veet'. With neuter nouns: hvitt (et hvitt hus).

what_colour.note: Also common: Hvilken farge har den?

this_one.note: When pointing, people often say denne her. For a neuter noun: dette.

that_one.note: For a neuter noun: det der. Further off: den der borte (that one over there).

another_one.note: For a neuter noun: ett til (ett glass til). Also: Kan jeg få en til?

its_hot.note: Varmt covers both warm and hot. Very hot: Det er kjempevarmt!

its_cold.note: The d is silent: 'kalt'. Freezing: Det er iskaldt!

its_sunny.note: Also: Sola skinner (the sun is shining).

its_windy.note: Literally 'it blows'. Also: Det er mye vind.

weather_today.note: Also: Hva slags vær er det i dag? The forecast: værmeldingen.

beautiful_day.note: Also: Det er en fin dag. About the weather: Så fint vær!

summer.note: In summer: om sommeren. This summer: i sommer.

winter.note: In winter: om vinteren. This winter: i vinter.

have_reservation.note: Also: Jeg har en reservasjon. Then give your name: på navnet Smith.

luggage.note: Say 'ba-GAH-sheh'. Suitcase: koffert. Hand luggage: håndbagasje.

wifi_password.note: Also common: Hva er passordet til nettet? (the network)

check_out_time.note: Hotels call it utsjekking. Check-in: innsjekking.

bus.note: Double s. Bus stop: bussholdeplass, or just holdeplass.

next_train.note: Trains and buses 'go' (går) in Norwegian. Tog sounds like 'tawg'.

is_this_seat_free.note: Shorter: Er det ledig her? Ledig means available; gratis means free of charge.

what_do_you_do.note: Also: Hva driver du med? Hva gjør du? usually means what are you doing right now.

i_work_in.note: For a place: i en bank. For a field, use med: Jeg jobber med salg.

im_student.note: Same for a woman. Jobs take no article: Jeg er lærer. A school pupil: elev.

meeting.note: Say 'MØ-teh'. I'm in a meeting: Jeg sitter i møte.

im_busy.note: Opptatt also means occupied, e.g. a toilet. Swamped: Jeg har mye å gjøre.

day_off.note: I'm off today: Jeg har fri i dag.

colleague.note: Same word for a woman. Plural: kolleger or kollegaer.

lets_start.note: Very common: Skal vi sette i gang? Casual: Da kjører vi!

good_job.note: Often said and written Bra jobba! Also: Godt jobbet!

table_for_two.note: Also: Kan vi få et bord til to? If you booked: Vi har bestilt bord.

not_spicy.note: Sterk means both strong and spicy. Not too spicy: ikke for sterkt.

more_water.note: Also: Kan vi få litt mer vann? Tap water: springvann.

no_sugar.note: Black coffee: svart kaffe. With milk: med melk.

im_full.note: Stuffed: Jeg er stappmett! After a meal at someone's home, say Takk for maten.

takeaway.note: Staff often ask: Spise her eller ta med? (eat in or take away?)

it_was_delicious.note: Also: Det smakte nydelig! Casual: Det var kjempegodt!

keep_change.note: Also: Det er greit sånn. Tipping is not expected in Norway.

head.note: Say 'HOO-deh'. In casual speech often shortened to 'hue': Jeg har vondt i hue.

stomach.note: Say 'MAH-geh'. Stomach ache: vondt i magen.

head_hurts.note: Works for any pain: Jeg har vondt i magen (stomach). Headache: hodepine.

medicine.note: Stress on the end: me-di-SEEN. Prescription: resept.

call_ambulance.note: The ambulance number in Norway is 113. People often just shout: Ring 113!

need_rest.note: The h in hvile is silent: 'VEE-leh'. Also: Jeg må slappe av (relax).

feel_better.note: Also very common: Det går bedre nå.

lets_meet.note: Suggestions are often questions with skal vi. Also: Skal vi ta en kaffe en dag?

are_you_free.note: Also: Er du ledig i morgen?

call_me.note: Gjerne makes it a friendly invitation. Text me: Send meg en melding.

your_number.note: Shorter and very common: Hva er nummeret ditt?

have_nice_day.note: To return the wish: Takk, i like måte! (same to you)

good_luck.note: Y is like German ü: 'LÜK-keh til'.

happy_birthday.note: Literally 'congratulations on the day'. Also: Gratulerer med fødselsdagen!

thanks_a_lot.note: Also: Mange takk. Extra warm: Tusen hjertelig takk!

miss_you.note: To several people: Jeg savner dere.
